headline: Aircraft Trace Europe’s Shared Fire Line
deck: The EU sent seven planes and four helicopters into France, then six planes, 134 firefighters and 41 vehicles into Spain. A new heat pulse is testing both fronts at once.
body: Europe’s wildfire front now has an air-traffic plan. The EU Civil Protection Mechanism sent seven planes and four helicopters from seven countries to France, while six planes, 134 firefighters and 41 vehicles went to Spain. A liaison officer joined the French command in Bordeaux, and Copernicus supplied emergency mapping to both countries. [E1]

The deployments connect fires that local commands still describe separately. Gironde’s Saumos front and Spain’s operations around Burgohondo, west of Madrid and in Castellón all drew on the shared response. [E1] Crews made enough progress for selective returns, but no continent-wide all-clear followed the aircraft.

Mutual aid is doing what it was built to do. Czech, Croatian, German, Portuguese, Slovak, Swedish and Turkish aircraft reinforced France; European crews and machines also entered Spain. [E1] The counter-case is therefore important: a long list of foreign tail numbers proves coordination, not failure. No official source in the Record says either national service exhausted its own fleet.

Pressure appears in the overlap. The European Commission counted more than 300,000 people displaced across the French and Spanish emergencies by Monday. [E1] The Joint Research Centre had already measured 254,388 hectares burned across the EU by 22 July and mapped very extreme danger over southwest France. [E2] Aircraft can cross a border in hours. Burned forest and evacuated towns remain after the sortie lands.

Tuesday’s operational gains arrived before Wednesday’s weather test. France placed sixteen departments under orange heat vigilance from noon on 29 July, including Gironde and Landes. [E3] Spain’s meteorological service measured soil moisture near three per cent in the Madrid–Ávila belt. [E4] Madrid emergency managers reported positive overnight work on one sector while warning that temperatures would rise. [E5]

The boring null is a severe seasonal cluster whose fires remain locally unrelated. Heat, dry ground and simultaneous demand can produce the same map without a single continental mechanism. The discriminator is logistical: whether France and Spain keep borrowing from the shared fleet at the same time, or release aircraft as perimeters move from active to controlled.

Quiet edges are not contained edges. The next break would force commanders to choose which plume keeps the plane already overhead and which plume waits for another border crossing. Europe’s shared fire line is visible in the routes between them.
